patch.value: Canonicalize dual beads/todos package implementations and define external-package dependency-range policy

Canonical home decided per package (extend an existing implementation, never a third); non-canonical repo README points to the canonical package and repo is archived or repurposed; capability divergence documented (external pm-beads import+export+validate+diff+bead_id schema vs in-repo import-only) with migration note; ecosystem dependency-range convention documented (caret year-range with verified floor; no exact pins, no unbounded >=) and pm-ops exact-pin 2026.7.13 plus pm-beads >=2026.7.10 ranges fixed; floor-verification folded into the reusable ecosystem smoke harness or the pm-o8um Verified-tier checklist

## Evidence (review pass #90, 2026-07-15)

Two pm extension packages exist as TWO independent live implementations each, with no canonical pointer:

- **beads**: external npm `pm-beads@2026.7.13` (unscoped, repo unbraind/pm-beads, installs via `pm install github.com/unbraind/pm-beads --global`; capabilities: import + export + `beads-validate`/`beads-diff` commands + `bead_id` schema field) vs in-repo `packages/pm-beads` (`@unbrained/pm-beads@2026.7.15`, private:true, first-party catalog, import-only per README). Divergent feature sets, divergent versions, different package identities.
- **todos**: external npm `pm-todos@2026.7.11` (unscoped, repo unbraind/pm-todos) vs in-repo `packages/pm-todos` (`@unbrained/pm-todos@2026.7.15`, private:true). Closed items pm-13bn (registerImporter/Exporter migration) and pm-ybfj (beads/todos runtime dedupe) only ever touched the in-repo pair.

Agents/users can install either implementation and get different behavior; fixes land in one and not the other.

## Dependency-range spread across the 18 external pm-* repos (verified 2026-07-15)

- Floors span `^2026.7.5` → `^2026.7.13`; floors are not verified against the API surface actually used (caret on date-based versions floats within the year, so most resolve to latest — the floor is documentation, currently unaudited).
- `pm-ops` pins exact `2026.7.13` (never floats → guaranteed staleness).
- external `pm-beads` uses unbounded `>=2026.7.10` (silently crosses the 2027 year-major boundary).

## Fix direction

Pick the canonical home per package (extend, never a third implementation), archive/redirect the other, document capability parity + migration. Define one ecosystem range convention (caret year-range with a floor verified by the pm-vnjh reusable smoke harness or the pm-o8um Verified-tier checks) and fix the two outliers.

## Cleared this pass (do not re-investigate)

External consumers (pm-graph/pm-web/pm-github/pm-changelog + companion examples) import ONLY official subpaths (`./sdk`, `./sdk/runtime`, `./sdk/testing`) — no deep `dist/` imports anywhere in the org; pm-graph's SDK imports are type-only.

External-package dependency-range census 2026-07-25 (evening ecosystem review), read live from the unbraind org via the GitHub contents API, covering the eight most recently updated public pm packages. This is the concrete evidence base this item's range-policy half has been missing.

Package | version | declared peer on @unbrained/pm-cli | pm.catalog | test script
pm-jira | 2026.7.25 | >=2026.7.10 | yes | yes
pm-linear | 2026.7.25 | >=2026.7.20 | yes | yes
pm-csv | 2026.7.25 | >=2026.7.19 | yes | yes
pm-context | 2026.7.25 | >=2026.7.10 | NO | yes
pm-brief | 2026.7.25 | NONE DECLARED | yes | yes
pm-gantt-chart | 2026.7.25 | >=2026.7.10 | yes | yes
pm-ts-starter | 2026.7.25 | >=2026.7.6 | yes | yes
pm-web | 2026.7.25 | NONE DECLARED | yes | yes

What is healthy: date-based version lockstep holds perfectly — all eight are on 2026.7.25, matching root. Every one ships a test script. So the release-versioning policy is working and this item's remaining scope is genuinely the RANGE policy, not versioning.

What this item owns, now quantified:
(1) Every declared peer range is unbounded (>=), and the floors are all DIFFERENT and apparently arbitrary — 2026.7.6, 2026.7.10 (three packages), 2026.7.19, 2026.7.20. Nothing indicates these floors were chosen against an actual SDK-compatibility boundary; they read as "whatever the CLI version was on authoring day". An unbounded upper edge means any future breaking SDK change silently satisfies the range on every one of these packages at once.
(2) Two packages, pm-brief and pm-web, declare NO peer dependency on @unbrained/pm-cli at all, so their SDK compatibility is unrecorded and unenforceable.
(3) pm-context declares no pm.catalog block, so it is the odd one out for catalog discovery.

Upstream cause worth fixing at the same time: the scaffold itself mints this pattern. `pm package init` generates peerDependencies {"@unbrained/pm-cli": ">=2026.6.24"} — an unbounded range with a hardcoded, already-stale floor — so every new package starts non-compliant with whatever policy this item lands. Scaffold divergence more broadly is pm-9smp7j.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Public-export-map dogfooding census 2026-07-25, relevant to this item's canonicalisation question. Of the fifteen first-party packages, ten contain their own PM_CLI_PACKAGE_ROOT-based loader that joins dist/sdk paths and dynamic-imports the result: pm-beads (runtime.ts and runtime-loader.ts), pm-todos (both), pm-calendar, pm-governance-audit, pm-guide-shell, pm-linked-test-adapters, pm-search-advanced, pm-templates. Only pm-calendar, pm-search-advanced and pm-governance-audit import runtime values through the public @unbrained/pm-cli/sdk/runtime subpath at all, and two of those do it alongside the private loader rather than instead of it.

The boundary itself is correct and documented (docs/EXTENSIONS.md:429, docs/SDK.md:1937): PM_CLI_PACKAGE_ROOT is first-party-only because bundled packages must find the running CLI before they are published independently. The observation is about what that costs, not about the rule. The packages best placed to catch a regression in the published export map — the ones built, tested and released in the same commit as the SDK — largely do not exercise it. A breaking change to the exports field in package.json would pass the full first-party suite.

This bears on the external-package canonicalisation this item tracks in a specific way: when pm-beads or pm-todos is reconciled against its external unscoped npm twin, the in-repo version cannot simply be published, because its runtime resolution depends on an environment variable no published package may read. Whatever canonicalisation lands has to answer how the same source resolves the SDK in both positions. The reusable-loader half of that is filed as pm-w7mqzt; the range and naming policy stays here.
